function: SIM-based electromagnetic neural network learns amplitudes and phases of transmitter and receiver stacked metasurfaces for end-to-end joint source-channel coding and image reconstruction (pp. 5-7)
system: Single transmit antenna feeding a transmitter SIM; N×N Rician channel to a receiver SIM; stacked RIS (3-9 layers, N=784 elements per layer); 28 GHz (pp. 3-4, 7-8)
method: End-to-end backpropagation training (Adam, MSE loss, 100 epochs, batch 64) of SIM amplitudes and phases as weights of an electromagnetic neural network with residual connections (pp. 6-7)
data_channel: MNIST (60,000 train, 10,000 test), also Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10; custom block Rician channel (K=3 dB, path-loss exponent 2.8, 10 m); Rayleigh-Sommerfeld diffraction between layers (pp. 3-4, 7, 11)
test_conditions: Trained at Pt = 60 dBm; tested on held-out MNIST for Pt -10 to 90 dBm and channel estimation error -30 to -15 dB (pp. 7, 10)
baselines: Non-learned: SIM with random phases and amplitudes; learned: digital DeepJSCC of [1] (Table 1) and SIM trained without residual connection (ablation) (pp. 9, 11-12)
metrics: PSNR and LPIPS of reconstructed images versus SNR, SIM layers, elements per layer, phase bits and channel estimation error; training MSE; processing time (pp. 8-12)
complexity: Processing time 0.29 ns per encoder or decoder versus 0.39 and 0.37 ms for digital DeepJSCC (Table 1); no FLOPs or parameter count; energy qualitative (pp. 11-12)
openness: none; MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 are public image sets, but no code or channel data link is given
q1_support: p. 4: "the wireless channel exhibits block fading and follows the Rician fading"; custom Rician model with a simple path loss (p. 7), no standardized (3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO) or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 7: "In the test phase, performance is evaluated by varying Pt from -10 to 90 dBm"; only SNR and channel-error sweeps on held-out MNIST, and each dataset uses its own N (p. 11).
q3_support: p. 11: "the conventional digital approach outperforms the proposed scheme, achieving a PSNR increase of 10.32 dB" (learned DeepJSCC [1]); p. 9: "a SIM with unoptimized random phases and amplitudes" (non-learned), both compared on PSNR and LPIPS.
q4_support: p. 11: "the proposed SIM-based system achieves a processing time of approximately 0.3 ns"; Table 1 (p. 12) gives 0.29 ns for the encoder and the decoder against 0.39 and 0.37 ms for digital DeepJSCC.
q5_support: p. 7: "we use the MNIST dataset [39] to evaluate the performance of the proposed SIM-based EMNN"; a public dataset of the learning task alone, with no code or channel data link.
notes: Borderline on function, for the reviewer to confirm: the learned parameters are the amplitudes and phases of the stacked RIS at both ends, trained end-to-end for image JSCC, with no beamforming, detection or channel-estimation objective. Included as area 3 because the learned output is the RIS phase and amplitude configuration; exclude with function if JSCC through SIM weights is judged not to be RIS configuration. q3=1 uses the random-phase SIM as non-learned baseline and digital DeepJSCC [1] as learned baseline (it wins by 10.32 dB PSNR). q4=1 rests on the 0.29 ns processing time (Table 1), which the text attributes to wave propagation and cites from [38], [44], so it is not a runtime measured by the authors; the reviewer may overrule.
